svg.aria-label: Ten users drawn across one day, each as a few short session blocks scattered over twenty-four hours. A vertical line marks a single instant at about midday, and it crosses exactly one of the ten sessions. That is the concurrency ratio: at any one moment only a small fraction of a day's users are inside the application. The arithmetic follows: a ceiling of five thousand two hundred and fifty concurrent users corresponds to roughly twenty-five to thirty thousand daily users at a five to ten percent concurrency ratio. The closing caption warns that the number to carry is 0.1 requests per second per user, because the concurrency headline is derived from a think-time model your own application probably does not share.
